roadmap.title: AI as your briefing and analysis staff
items: Have AI summarise staff reports, board papers and market news into one-page briefs, and ask for the sources behind key claims.

roadmap.title: Lead what only leaders can
items: Spend the time saved on people: board relationships, key hires, culture.

roadmap.project: Hold a leadership session on how AI changes your business model, and agree on three strategic decisions with owners and dates.

items: Use AI for spelling, grammar and consistency checks, then review its changes; it misses context and voice.
Ask AI to suggest structure and readability edits on long manuscripts, and decide which to keep.
Use AI to check facts, dates and figures against sources you name.
roadmap.project: Edit 10 pieces with an AI first pass, track which suggestions you accepted or rejected, and compare total editing time.

roadmap.title: A house style the tools follow
items: Turn your style guide into prompts and checklists the AI tools use every time.
Set clear rules for authors and staff on AI-written text and disclosure.
Build templates for briefs, newsletters and recurring content.
roadmap.project: Write your publication's AI style and disclosure guide, test it on five pieces, and revise it with your team.

roadmap.title: Grow judgement and team leadership
items: Focus on what to publish and why: the editorial choices AI cannot make.
Coach writers and reporters, and give feedback that improves their next piece.
Look at related roles: managing editor, content strategist, or publisher.
roadmap.project: Plan one issue or content series from idea to publication, and document the editorial decisions you made and why.

aiTools: AI writing and grammar assistants (e.g. Grammarly, built-in editors)
ChatGPT or Claude for structure and readability suggestions
Fact-checking and plagiarism tools
humanEdge: Deciding what is worth publishing
Protecting the author's voice and the publication's standards
Coaching writers and running deadlines

roadmap.title: Faster editing and culling
items: Use AI culling and auto-adjust features in Lightroom or similar tools to sort and correct large shoots.
Use AI masking and retouching for skin, backgrounds and objects, and check the result at full size.
Draft client emails, quotes and booking confirmations with AI.
roadmap.project: Edit one full shoot with AI culling and masking, compare the time with a similar past shoot, and note what you had to redo.

roadmap.title: Run the business on templates
items: Use booking and invoicing software with automatic reminders.
Create presets and AI-assisted workflows for your typical shoots.
Write clear rules with clients on AI retouching and generated content.
roadmap.project: Set up automatic booking, reminder and invoice emails, and measure the admin hours per week before and after a month.

roadmap.title: Grow the part that happens behind the camera
items: Strengthen the shoot itself: directing people, light and timing, which AI cannot be present for.
Build a recognisable style and the client relationships that bring repeat work.
Look at related roles: video, art direction, or graphic design.
roadmap.project: Do a personal project of 10 portraits or scenes focused on one lighting or directing skill, and share it in your portfolio.

aiTools: Lightroom and Photoshop AI features (masking, denoise, generative fill)

Never enter identifiable patient data into public AI tools.
roadmap.project: Write plain-language counselling notes for 10 common medicines with AI help, check them against official sources, and use them for a month.

roadmap.title: Smoother pharmacy operations
items: Use your pharmacy system to automate stock reorders and expiry alerts.

Build checklists for controlled-drug records and audits.
roadmap.project: Set up automatic reorder and expiry alerts for your top 50 products and track stock-outs for two months.

roadmap.title: Grow clinical and patient care
items: Spend more time on medication reviews and helping patients manage chronic conditions.

Never enter identifiable patient details into public AI tools.

roadmap.project: Track home-care follow-through for 15 patients over three months after giving them personalised advice, and note what worked.
